lessons.title: Enterprise access model for privileged roles
lessons.short: The enterprise access model replaces the old AD tier model with a control plane, a management plane and a data/workload plane, plus user and app access pathways. Privileged roles are assigned and delegated so lower planes can never control higher ones.
lessons.deep:
Microsoft's **enterprise access model** evolves the AD **Tier 0/1/2** model for hybrid and multicloud:
- **Control plane** (expanded Tier 0): identity and access control for the whole enterprise: Entra ID Global Administrator and Privileged Role Administrator, AD DS domain controllers, Entra Connect, AD FS, AD CS, PIM, Conditional Access, and network access control where it's the only control (OT).
- **Management plane** (part of Tier 1): enterprise-wide IT management, such as subscription owners and Intune admins.
- **Data/workload plane** (part of Tier 1): per-workload and per-app administration, often by DevOps teams.
- **User access** and **app access** (former Tier 2): employees, partners, customers and APIs.

**Design principles for role assignment and delegation**
- Lower planes must never control higher planes (no Tier 1 admin can reset a Tier 0 password or edit a Tier 0 GPO).
- **Least privilege**: built-in roles with the smallest scope, such as User Administrator, Helpdesk Administrator, or **administrative units** to scope by region, instead of Global Administrator.
- **Just-in-time** elevation with PIM; few permanent assignments.
- Separate admin accounts (cloud-only for Entra privileged roles), used only from **PAWs**.
- Azure: assign at management group/subscription only when needed; delegate resource-group scope to workload teams.
- Keep two or more **emergency access** accounts.

terms.d: Enterprise access model plane holding identity and access control systems (expanded Tier 0).
Plane for enterprise-wide IT management functions.
Entra container that scopes directory role assignments to a subset of users, groups or devices.
Break-glass cloud-only Global Administrator account for lockout recovery.

lessons.trap: Entra Connect servers, AD CS and PIM belong to the control plane (Tier 0), not the management plane; treating them as ordinary servers is the common error.
lessons.example: A regional helpdesk gets Helpdesk Administrator scoped to an 'EMEA users' administrative unit instead of User Administrator tenant-wide.

lessons.title: Privileged Identity Management (PIM)
lessons.short: Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management gives just-in-time, time-bound, approval-based activation of Entra roles, Azure resource roles and group membership (PIM for Groups). Eligible assignments are activated on demand with MFA or authentication context, justification and approval.
lessons.deep:
**PIM** (Entra ID P2 or Entra ID Governance) removes standing privilege.

**Assignment types**
- **Eligible**: user must activate before using the role.
- **Active**: role is usable immediately (keep for emergency access only).
- Both can be permanent or time-bound (start/end dates).

**Role settings (per role)**
- **Activation maximum duration**: 1–24 hours.
- On activation require **MFA** or a **Conditional Access authentication context** (for example, phishing-resistant MFA from a PAW).
- Require **justification**, **ticket information** (not validated) and **approval** (choose explicit approvers).
- Notifications and alerts (for example, roles assigned outside PIM).

**Scope**
- Microsoft Entra roles, **Azure resource roles** (management group to resource), and **PIM for Groups** (just-in-time membership or ownership of a security group, which can carry app access or role-assignable roles).

**Audit and review**
- PIM audit history and **access reviews** of role assignments.
- Requires Privileged Role Administrator to configure Entra role settings.

PIM controls *activation*; protect the *use* of a role with a CA policy scoped to directory roles or protected actions.

terms.d: PIM assignment that must be activated before the role can be used.
Just-in-time membership or ownership of security groups.
How long an activation lasts, 1 to 24 hours.
PIM setting requiring a named approver before activation succeeds.

lessons.trap: PIM's MFA-on-activation doesn't protect a role after activation or for permanent active assignments; the fix combines eligible assignments with CA or protected actions.
lessons.example: Exchange Administrators are eligible for up to 4 hours, must satisfy authentication context c2 (phishing-resistant MFA on a compliant device) and need approval from the messaging lead.

lessons.title: Entitlement management and Entra ID Governance
lessons.short: Entitlement management bundles groups, apps, SharePoint sites and roles into access packages with request, approval, expiry and review policies, including for external users from connected organizations. Microsoft Entra ID Governance adds lifecycle workflows and advanced features beyond Entra ID P2.
lessons.deep:
**Entitlement management** (identity governance) automates access request workflows.
- **Catalog**: a container of resources and access packages, delegated to catalog owners.
- **Access package**: groups/teams, applications, SharePoint sites (and in preview, Entra roles) assigned together.
- **Policies**: who can request (internal users, specific **connected organizations**, any external user), approval stages, requestor questions, **expiration**, **separation of duties** (incompatible packages) and recurring **access reviews**.
- External users get a B2B guest account on approval; when their last assignment expires, the guest can be blocked and removed automatically.

**Licensing**
- **Entra ID P2**: PIM, access reviews (core), entitlement management (basic).
- **Microsoft Entra ID Governance** (requires P1 or P2): **lifecycle workflows** (joiner/mover/leaver), custom extensions (Logic Apps), **Verified ID** in access packages, auto-assignment policies, machine-learning-assisted access reviews, inactive-user reviews, PIM for Groups reviews, and integration with ID Protection and Purview Insider Risk Management.
- New IGA features are released in ID Governance, not P2.

**Lifecycle workflows** automate tasks such as generating a Temporary Access Pass before day one, or removing groups and licences at departure.

terms.d: Bundle of resource roles requested and assigned together with a policy.
External directory or domain whose users may request access packages.
ID Governance automation for joiner, mover and leaver tasks.
Access package check that blocks incompatible combinations.

lessons.trap: Lifecycle workflows and Verified ID requirements in access packages need Entra ID Governance, not just P2.
lessons.example: A supplier is added as a connected organization; its staff request a 'Supplier portal' package approved by a sponsor, expiring after 90 days with a quarterly review.

lessons.title: AD DS security, governance and attack resilience
lessons.short: Evaluate AD DS against common attacks: pass-the-hash, pass-the-ticket, Kerberoasting, DCSync, Golden Ticket and AD CS abuse. Resilience comes from tiering, credential hygiene, Defender for Identity detections, lateral movement path reviews and a tested forest recovery plan.
lessons.deep:
**Common AD DS attacks and mitigations**
- **Pass-the-hash / pass-the-ticket**: reuse of cached credentials. Mitigate with tiered logon restrictions, **Credential Guard**, **Windows LAPS**, Protected Users, and no Tier 0 logons on workstations.
- **Kerberoasting**: requesting service tickets for accounts with SPNs and cracking them offline. Mitigate with **gMSA** or 25+ character passwords and AES-only encryption.
- **AS-REP roasting**: accounts without Kerberos pre-authentication. Require pre-auth.
- **DCSync / DCShadow**: abuse of replication rights. Restrict replication permissions to DCs; detect with **Defender for Identity**.
- **Golden Ticket**: forged TGTs signed with the **krbtgt** key. Protect DCs as Tier 0; reset krbtgt twice after compromise.
- **AD CS abuse (ESC-style)**: misconfigured templates allow requesting certificates as any user. Review templates and enrolment rights; monitor AD CS with MDI sensors.
- **Password spray / brute force**: fine-grained password policies, smart lockout, and MFA on remote access.

**Governance**
- Regular reviews of privileged groups and **lateral movement paths** (shown in Defender for Identity).
- Identity security posture assessments in **Microsoft Secure Score / Exposure Management**.
- Resilience: protected offline DC backups, documented **AD forest recovery**, and the ability to operate if Entra Connect or AD FS is lost.

terms.d: Offline cracking of service tickets for accounts with service principal names.
Abusing directory replication rights to pull password hashes from a DC.
Forged Kerberos TGT made with the stolen krbtgt key.
Chain of sessions and admin rights an attacker could follow to sensitive accounts.

lessons.trap: Resetting the krbtgt password once doesn't invalidate a Golden Ticket because the previous key is still accepted; it must be reset twice (with replication time between).
lessons.example: Defender for Identity flags a lateral movement path from a helpdesk PC to a Domain Admin; the fix is removing the admin's interactive sessions on Tier 2 devices.

lessons.title: Secure administration of cloud tenants, SaaS and multicloud
lessons.short: Secure tenant administration uses cloud-only admin accounts, phishing-resistant MFA, PIM, emergency access accounts, protected actions and admin portals reached only from PAWs. In multicloud and SaaS, federate admin access to Entra ID and monitor admin activity centrally.
lessons.deep:
**Microsoft 365 and Entra tenant**
- **Cloud-only** accounts for Entra privileged roles (not synced from AD DS, so an on-premises compromise can't take over the cloud).
- Fewer than five Global Administrators; at least **two emergency access accounts** excluded from most CA but protected with FIDO2 and monitored with alerts.
- **PIM** for all privileged roles; **phishing-resistant MFA** authentication strength for admin roles.
- **Protected actions** for CA policy changes, cross-tenant settings and hard deletes.
- Restrict access to admin portals and Microsoft Graph PowerShell; review **app consent** and high-privilege app permissions.

**Azure**
- Management group hierarchy with least-privilege RBAC; PIM for Owner/User Access Administrator; **Azure Policy** guardrails; Activity log to Sentinel.

**Multicloud and SaaS**
- Federate AWS IAM Identity Center and Google Cloud admin access to Entra ID; avoid AWS root and long-lived IAM user keys.
- Use **Defender for Cloud** CSPM/CIEM for AWS and GCP posture and over-permissioned identities.
- Use **Defender for Cloud Apps** SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) and app connectors for admin activity in Salesforce, ServiceNow and others.
- MSPs use **GDAP** (granular delegated admin privileges) for Microsoft 365 customer tenants and **Azure Lighthouse** for Azure.

terms.d: Granular delegated admin privileges: least-privilege, time-bound partner access to customer tenants.
Privileged account created in Entra ID, not synced from AD DS.
SaaS security posture management, for example in Defender for Cloud Apps.

lessons.trap: Syncing on-premises Domain Admins to be Global Administrators is wrong; cloud privileged roles should be held by cloud-only accounts.
lessons.example: An MSP moves from legacy DAP to GDAP with time-bound Helpdesk Administrator access, and the customer's Global Administrators are cloud-only accounts with FIDO2 keys.

lessons.title: Cloud infrastructure entitlement management (CIEM)
lessons.short: CIEM finds and right-sizes excessive permissions held by human and workload identities across Azure, AWS and GCP. Microsoft Entra Permissions Management was retired in 2025; Microsoft now provides CIEM in the Defender CSPM plan of Microsoft Defender for Cloud.
lessons.deep:
In multicloud, identities accumulate permissions they never use: an AWS role with `*:*`, a GCP service account with Owner, an Azure service principal with Contributor on a subscription. **CIEM** (cloud infrastructure entitlement management) addresses this gap between **granted** and **used** permissions.

Capabilities to design for:
- **Discovery** of identities and entitlements across Azure (Entra users, groups, service principals), AWS (IAM users, roles, groups) and GCP (IAM users, groups, service accounts).
- **Usage analytics**: compare granted permissions with activity to find **overprovisioned** and **inactive** identities.
- **Recommendations**: remove inactive or guest identities with access, limit admin privileges, right-size roles, enforce MFA for IAM users.
- **Attack path** context: an over-permissioned identity combined with an exposed VM appears in **attack path analysis** and **cloud security explorer**.

**Product status (verify dates in questions carefully)**
- **Microsoft Entra Permissions Management** was retired: no longer sold from April 2025, support ended **1 October 2025**.
- Microsoft recommends **Defender CSPM** in Defender for Cloud for CIEM; third-party CIEM tools are an option for deeper needs.

Pair CIEM with PIM for Azure roles and federated, time-bound access in AWS and GCP.

terms.d: Cloud infrastructure entitlement management: discovering and right-sizing cloud permissions.
Identity granted far more permissions than it uses.
Paid Defender for Cloud posture plan including CIEM, attack paths and cloud security explorer.

lessons.trap: Recommending a new deployment of Microsoft Entra Permissions Management is wrong after its retirement; the current Microsoft answer is Defender CSPM.
lessons.example: Defender CSPM shows a GCP service account with Owner that has only read from one bucket in 90 days; the team replaces Owner with a custom read-only role.

lessons.title: Evaluating access review solutions
lessons.short: Access reviews periodically ask reviewers to confirm whether users, guests or service principals still need group, app, access package or privileged role access. Evaluate scope, reviewers, recurrence, decision helpers and auto-apply results against compliance requirements.
lessons.deep:
**What can be reviewed**
- Group and Microsoft 365 group/Teams membership, application assignments, **access package assignments**, **Entra roles and Azure resource roles in PIM**, and (Governance) PIM for Groups and catalog reviews.

**Design choices**
- **Reviewers**: resource owners, managers, selected users, or **self-review**. Multi-stage reviews add a second stage, for example manager then app owner.
- **Scope**: all users, guests only, or (Governance) inactive users only.
- **Recurrence**: weekly to annually; duration of each instance.
- **Decision helpers**: last sign-in recommendations; machine-learning-assisted recommendations based on peer similarity (Governance).
- **Upon completion**: **auto-apply results** to remove denied users; action if reviewers don't respond (remove access, approve, take recommendations).
- For guests: block sign-in for 30 days then delete when removed from all access.

**Licensing**: Entra ID P2 for core reviews; Entra ID Governance for ML-assisted, inactive-user-only and PIM for Groups reviews.

**Evaluating fit**: Microsoft-native reviews cover Entra-integrated resources. For non-Entra resources, use custom data provided resource reviews or a third-party IGA solution, and Defender for Cloud CIEM for cloud infrastructure permissions.

Audit evidence: review history and downloadable results support SOX, ISO 27001 and similar audits.

terms.d: Recurring attestation of who should keep access to a resource.
Setting that removes denied access automatically when a review ends.
Review with sequential reviewer stages.
Users attest to their own continued need for access.

lessons.trap: Without auto-apply, denied decisions aren't enforced automatically; an answer that 'creates a review' but never applies results misses the requirement.
lessons.example: A quarterly multi-stage review of the payments app uses managers then app owners, removes non-responders, and auto-applies results to satisfy SOX evidence.

lessons.title: Privileged access workstations (PAW)
lessons.short: A privileged access workstation is a hardened, Intune-managed device used only for administration: no email or general browsing, application control enforced, no local admin, and hardware-backed security. Microsoft defines enterprise, specialized and privileged device profiles.
lessons.deep:
Admins are only as secure as the device they type on. Microsoft's **device security profiles**:
- **Enterprise**: standard productivity device with Defender for Endpoint and security baselines.
- **Specialized**: no local admin, only admin-deployed apps (application control enforced), email and browsing still allowed.
- **Privileged (PAW)**: highest protection for roles whose compromise would materially harm the organization.

**PAW requirements**
- **Email and general web browsing blocked**; deny-by-default URL allow list.
- Managed by **Intune** with security baselines and **Defender for Endpoint**; deployed with **Windows Autopilot** to a known-good state; no BYOD.
- **Application control** (AppLocker/App Control for Business) enforced; apps only via Intune.
- **No local admin rights**.
- Hardware root of trust: **TPM 2.0**, UEFI Secure Boot, virtualization-based security, **Credential Guard**, BitLocker.
- Separate admin account; admins use a different device or account for productivity.

**Enforcing PAW use**: a Conditional Access policy with a **device filter** (for example, extensionAttribute or a PAW device group) or compliant-device requirement for admin roles; combine with PIM authentication context and protected actions.

Cloud PCs (Windows 365) can be configured as privileged workstations where physical PAWs are impractical, if hardened to the same profile.

terms.d: Privileged access workstation: hardened device dedicated to administrative tasks.
Locked-down device without local admin that still allows email and browsing.
Conditional Access condition targeting devices by attributes such as extensionAttribute1.
Cloud-based provisioning that resets new devices to a managed, known-good state.

lessons.trap: A PAW that still allows Outlook and web browsing is a specialized device, not a PAW; and a jump server alone doesn't protect credentials typed on an unmanaged laptop.
lessons.example: Global Administrators can activate roles only from devices with extensionAttribute1 = 'PAW', enforced by a Conditional Access device filter.

lessons.title: Secure remote administration: Bastion and just-in-time VM access
lessons.short: Remote administration should never expose RDP or SSH to the internet. Use Azure Bastion for browser or native-client RDP/SSH over TLS without public IPs, just-in-time VM access in Defender for Servers Plan 2 to open ports briefly, and Entra Private Access for on-premises servers.
lessons.deep:
**Azure Bastion**
- Managed PaaS deployed in the VNet's **AzureBastionSubnet**; admins connect over TLS 443 from the Azure portal or native client, and target VMs need **no public IP**.
- **Standard/Premium** SKUs add native client support, shareable links, IP-based connections and, on Premium, **session recording**.
- Combine with Entra ID sign-in to VMs and Conditional Access.

**Just-in-time (JIT) VM access**
- Part of **Defender for Servers Plan 2**.
- Locks management ports (3389, 22) with NSG or Azure Firewall rules; an approved request opens the port for a time window and only from the requester's IP.
- Requests are logged in the Activity log.

**On-premises and other clouds**
- **Microsoft Entra Private Access** gives per-app access to RDP/SSH targets with Conditional Access, replacing VPN.
- Admin access always from a **PAW**, possibly via a hardened **jump server** in the same tier.

**Design principles**: no inbound management ports from the internet; identity-based, time-bound access; recorded sessions for privileged work; separate management subnets with NSGs.

terms.d: Managed RDP/SSH broker over TLS so VMs need no public IP.
Defender for Servers Plan 2 feature that opens management ports only on approved request.
Dedicated subnet name required for Azure Bastion.

lessons.trap: JIT VM access needs Defender for Servers Plan 2, not Plan 1; and Bastion removes the need for public IPs on VMs, not the need for a PAW.
lessons.example: Ops engineers connect to production VMs only through Bastion Premium with session recording, from PAWs, after activating their PIM role.

questions.stem: You will deploy 200 instances of an autonomous procurement agent, all created from the same Microsoft Entra Agent ID blueprint. Any instance flagged high risk must be blocked, including instances created next year. What should the Conditional Access policy target?
options: All users
The agent identity blueprint
A security group containing the current agent identities
The Office 365 cloud app
questions.explain: A policy targeting the blueprint applies to every agent identity created from it, including future ones. 'All users' doesn't cover agents, a static group misses new instances (and group membership isn't how agent users are scoped), and targeting a resource doesn't express 'these agents'.

questions.case: Northwind builds an AI assistant that reads a user's mailbox on the user's behalf (delegated) and also runs nightly app-only jobs against SharePoint. Some downstream systems require the agent to have its own user account.
questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if true.

statements.s: For the delegated mailbox calls, Conditional Access policies targeting the signed-in user apply.
A Conditional Access policy assigned to 'All users' also covers the agent's user account.
The agent identity stores its own client secret, separate from the blueprint.

questions.explain: In on-behalf-of flows the token subject is the user, so user policies apply. Agent user accounts aren't covered by policies scoped through the Users assignment; you target them under Agents. Agent identities have no credentials of their own; the blueprint holds them.

questions.stem: A developer team wants its agent to call a third-party API using a static API key rather than Microsoft Entra tokens. Security requires Conditional Access to govern every agent call. What is the design issue?
options: API keys must be stored in Managed HSM rather than Key Vault
The agent must be assigned an Entra ID P2 licence
Calls using an API key bypass the Entra token pipeline, so Conditional Access can't evaluate them
API keys are only supported for agent user accounts
questions.explain: Conditional Access is evaluated when Entra ID issues tokens; an agent that authenticates with an API key never requests an Entra token, so policy can't apply. Storage location or licence doesn't change that, and API keys aren't an agent user feature.

questions.stem: A company wants to retire its VPN. Remote staff must reach an on-premises ERP (custom TCP protocol) and file shares, with Conditional Access requiring a compliant device. What should you recommend?
options: Microsoft Entra Application Proxy
Azure VPN Gateway point-to-site with certificate authentication
Microsoft Entra Internet Access
Microsoft Entra Private Access
questions.explain: Entra Private Access provides Zero Trust per-app access to private TCP/UDP apps and file shares with Conditional Access. Application Proxy publishes only web (HTTP/HTTPS) apps. A point-to-site VPN is what they're retiring and grants network-level access, and Internet Access secures traffic to internet and SaaS destinations.

questions.stem: Engineers use AWS and Google Cloud consoles with separate local accounts. You need one identity, MFA enforced by Conditional Access, and automatic deprovisioning when people leave. Which TWO capabilities should you use? Select TWO.
options: SAML single sign-on from Microsoft Entra ID to AWS IAM Identity Center and Google Cloud
SCIM provisioning from Microsoft Entra ID to those platforms
Azure Lighthouse delegation to the AWS account
Defender for Cloud agentless scanning
B2B direct connect with AWS
questions.explain: Federated SAML SSO brings sign-ins through Entra ID so Conditional Access and MFA apply, and SCIM provisioning creates and removes accounts automatically. Lighthouse manages Azure resources across tenants only, agentless scanning is a posture feature, and B2B direct connect works only between Entra tenants.

questions.stem: An Azure Function must read secrets from Azure Key Vault without any credential stored in code or configuration. What should it use?
options: A managed identity with the Key Vault Secrets User role
A client secret stored in app settings
A shared access signature (SAS) token
A storage account access key
questions.explain: A managed identity has no secret to store and can be granted the Key Vault Secrets User RBAC role. A client secret in app settings is a stored credential, and SAS tokens and storage account keys are for Azure Storage, not Key Vault.

questions.case: Adatum acquired a company whose Active Directory forest has no network connectivity or trust with Adatum's forest. Adatum wants the acquired users in its Microsoft Entra tenant within weeks, with no new sync servers to maintain and high availability for the sync service.
questions.stem: Which synchronization design should you recommend for the acquired forest?
options: Add the forest to the existing Microsoft Entra Connect Sync server
Use B2B collaboration invitations for all acquired users
Create a forest trust and then use Entra Connect Sync
Install Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync agents in the acquired forest
questions.explain: Cloud Sync handles disconnected forests natively with lightweight agents managed from the cloud, and multiple agents give high availability. Connect Sync needs line of sight to every forest it syncs, a trust adds time and risk, and B2B makes them guests rather than members of the tenant.

questions.stem: A company federates with AD FS and wants to reduce attack surface and keep cloud sign-in working if the datacenter is offline. Which TWO actions should you recommend? Select TWO.
options: Enable password hash synchronization
Migrate domains from federation to cloud authentication using staged rollout
Deploy additional AD FS servers in a second datacenter
Switch to pass-through authentication as the only method
Disable Seamless SSO
questions.explain: Password hash sync authenticates in the cloud, survives on-premises outages and enables leaked credential detection; staged rollout moves users off AD FS safely. More AD FS servers keep the golden-SAML attack surface, PTA still depends on on-premises agents, and disabling Seamless SSO doesn't address either goal.

questions.stem: For each statement about hybrid identity, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Password hash synchronization enables Microsoft Entra ID Protection to detect leaked credentials for synced users.
With pass-through authentication, an outage of all on-premises agents prevents cloud sign-in for those users.
Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync supports device writeback.

questions.explain: PHS gives Entra ID hashes to compare with leaked credential sets. PTA validates passwords on premises, so losing all agents breaks sign-in. Device writeback isn't supported by Cloud Sync (Microsoft points to Cloud Kerberos trust instead).

questions.stem: A GitHub Actions workflow deploys infrastructure to Azure. Security forbids storing any Azure credential in GitHub. What should you configure?
options: A service principal certificate uploaded as a GitHub secret
A system-assigned managed identity on the GitHub runner
A federated identity credential on an app registration, trusting the repository and branch
A personal access token for an Azure DevOps service connection
questions.explain: Workload identity federation lets GitHub's OIDC token be exchanged for an Entra token, so no secret is stored. A certificate in GitHub is still a stored credential, GitHub-hosted runners aren't Azure resources so can't have a system-assigned managed identity, and a PAT is a stored secret for a different service.

questions.stem: For each statement about Conditional Access for workload identities, select Yes if true.

statements.s: It requires Workload Identities Premium licensing to create or modify the policies.
It can enforce a policy on managed identities.
Block access is the grant control available for these policies.

questions.explain: Workload identity CA needs Workload Identities Premium, applies to single-tenant service principals registered in your tenant (not managed identities or multitenant SaaS apps), and its only grant control is Block access, triggered by location or service principal risk.

questions.case: Proseware runs 50 Linux servers in an on-premises datacenter and 30 in AWS. Scripts on these servers call Azure Storage and Key Vault using client secrets stored in config files. A recent incident leaked one secret. Proseware wants to eliminate secrets for these calls and manage the servers from Azure.
questions.stem: What should you recommend?
options: Onboard the servers to Azure Arc and use the Arc-enabled server's managed identity
Move the client secrets into environment variables
Replace client secrets with storage account keys rotated monthly
Create B2B guest accounts for each server
questions.explain: Azure Arc-enabled servers get a system-assigned managed identity that can be granted RBAC on Storage and Key Vault without secrets, and Arc also lets Azure manage them. Environment variables still hold secrets, account keys are even broader secrets, and guest accounts are for people from other organizations.

questions.stem: Partner users already complete MFA in their own Microsoft Entra tenant but are prompted again when accessing your apps as B2B guests. Your Conditional Access requires MFA for guests. What should you configure?
options: Inbound trust settings in cross-tenant access settings to trust MFA from the partner tenant
Exclude guest users from the MFA policy
Outbound access settings for the partner tenant
Tenant restrictions v2
questions.explain: Inbound trust settings let your tenant accept the partner's MFA claim, so your policy is satisfied without a second prompt. Excluding guests removes protection, outbound settings govern your users going to other tenants, and tenant restrictions v2 controls which external accounts your users can use on your devices.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Entra External ID, select Yes if true.

statements.s: B2B direct connect is blocked by default and must be enabled by both organizations.
B2B collaboration users are represented as guest user objects in the resource tenant.
By default, your tenant trusts MFA and compliant-device claims from all other Microsoft Entra organizations.

questions.explain: B2B direct connect requires mutual configuration and is off by default. B2B collaboration creates guest objects. Default inbound trust settings don't trust other organizations' MFA or device claims; you must enable trust explicitly.

questions.case: Woodgrove and its subsidiary run separate Microsoft Entra tenants. 3,000 subsidiary employees need to appear automatically as users in Woodgrove's tenant for Teams and apps, be removed when they leave, and not receive invitation emails or consent prompts.
questions.stem: What should you recommend?
options: Bulk B2B invitations with a PowerShell script each month
Microsoft Entra Connect Sync from the subsidiary's tenant
Cross-tenant synchronization with automatic redemption enabled in both tenants
B2B direct connect only
questions.explain: Cross-tenant synchronization automates creating and removing B2B users across tenants of a multitenant organization, and automatic redemption (both outbound and inbound) suppresses consent prompts. Scripted invites are manual and send emails, Entra Connect syncs from AD DS not from another tenant, and direct connect doesn't create user objects.

questions.stem: Help desk staff are being socially engineered into resetting MFA for impostors. You want callers to prove their identity with a credential issued after HR identity proofing, held in a wallet on their phone. What should you recommend?
options: Self-service password reset with security questions
SMS one-time passcode to the number on file
B2B collaboration with email one-time passcode
Microsoft Entra Verified ID verifiable credentials presented from Microsoft Authenticator
questions.explain: Verified ID lets the organization issue a verifiable credential that the employee holds in Authenticator and presents to the help desk verifier, which defeats impersonation. Security questions and SMS codes are weak and phishable, and B2B email OTP is a guest sign-in method rather than identity proofing.

questions.stem: Put the steps of a Microsoft Entra Verified ID exchange in order.
options: The issuer verifies the person and issues a signed verifiable credential
The holder stores the credential in Microsoft Authenticator
A verifier requests a presentation and the holder shares the credential
The verifier validates the signature against the issuer's decentralized identifier
questions.explain: The issuer signs and issues the credential, the holder keeps it in a wallet, the verifier requests it and the holder presents it, and finally the verifier checks the signature using the issuer's DID (did:web) without calling the issuer.

questions.stem: Which methods satisfy the built-in Phishing-resistant MFA authentication strength? Select THREE.
options: FIDO2 security key
Windows Hello for Business
Microsoft Authenticator push notification
Certificate-based authentication (multifactor)
SMS one-time passcode
questions.explain: The built-in Phishing-resistant MFA strength includes FIDO2 security keys, Windows Hello for Business or platform credentials, and multifactor certificate-based authentication. Authenticator push and SMS satisfy the general MFA strength but can be relayed by adversary-in-the-middle phishing.

questions.stem: Users may open a SharePoint site labelled Highly Confidential only after phishing-resistant MFA from a compliant device. Other sites need only standard MFA. What should you use to target the stricter policy?
options: A Conditional Access authentication context linked to the sensitivity label
A named location for the SharePoint site
A device filter on the Office 365 app
A separate tenant for the confidential site
questions.explain: Authentication context lets a CA policy apply to a specific resource, such as a SharePoint site whose sensitivity label references context c1. Named locations describe network origins, a device filter describes devices rather than content, and a separate tenant is unnecessary overhead.

questions.stem: You are reviewing a Conditional Access policy created through Microsoft Graph that must block legacy authentication clients. Complete the conditions section.
options: ["browser", "mobileAppsAndDesktopClients"]
["exchangeActiveSync", "other"]
["all"]
["browser"]
questions.explain: Legacy authentication clients are represented by the clientAppTypes values exchangeActiveSync and other. Browser and mobileAppsAndDesktopClients are modern authentication clients, so blocking them (or 'all') would block every user.

questions.stem: For each statement about continuous access evaluation (CAE), select Yes if true.

statements.s: A CAE-capable resource such as Exchange Online can reject a token soon after the user's account is disabled, before the token would normally expire.
CAE enforces country/region-based named locations in real time.
CAE-capable sessions can receive long-lived tokens of up to 28 hours.

questions.explain: CAE resources react to critical events such as account disablement. Real-time location enforcement works only with IP-based named locations; country locations aren't evaluated instantly. Because revocation is event-driven, CAE tokens can last up to 28 hours.

questions.stem: You must ensure that any administrator who creates, updates or deletes a Conditional Access policy first completes phishing-resistant MFA, no matter how they got the permission. What should you implement?
options: A PIM activation setting requiring MFA
A Conditional Access policy targeting the Conditional Access Administrator directory role
Protected actions mapped to a Conditional Access authentication context
An access review of Conditional Access Administrators
questions.explain: Protected actions attach an authentication context (and its CA policy) to specific permissions, enforced when the action is attempted regardless of role or how it was obtained. PIM enforces only at activation, a role-targeted policy misses custom roles or other paths, and access reviews don't enforce authentication.

questions.case: Relecloud still uses the legacy user risk and sign-in risk policies in Microsoft Entra ID Protection. It holds Entra ID P2. The security lead wants risk-based protection to continue past the legacy policy retirement and to follow Microsoft's current recommendations.
questions.stem: What should you recommend?
options: Create one Conditional Access policy combining user risk High and sign-in risk Medium with Block access
Separate CA policies (user risk High: risk remediation; sign-in risk Medium+High: MFA), then disable legacy
Keep the legacy policies and enable security defaults
Configure CAE strict location enforcement instead of risk policies
questions.explain: Microsoft recommends separate risk-based CA policies (not combined conditions): require risk remediation for high user risk and MFA for medium/high sign-in risk, tested in report-only, then disable the legacy policies, which retire on 1 October 2026. Blocking stops self-remediation, security defaults conflict with CA, and CAE doesn't replace risk policies.

questions.stem: You need to find successful sign-ins in the last 7 days where no Conditional Access policy applied, to discover gaps in your Zero Trust coverage. Complete the KQL query.
questions.code:
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ResultType == 0
| where ____ == "notApplied"
| summarize Count = count() by AppDisplayName, UserPrincipalName
options: RiskState
AuthenticationRequirement
ConditionalAccessStatus
ClientAppUsed
questions.explain: ConditionalAccessStatus records success, failure or notApplied for each sign-in. RiskState is ID Protection risk, AuthenticationRequirement shows single- or multifactor, and ClientAppUsed identifies the client type; none indicates whether a policy applied.

questions.case: During a Zero Trust review at Fourth Coffee you find: a 'Require MFA' policy excludes a 400-member 'VIP' group; legacy authentication isn't blocked; admin roles accept any MFA method; two emergency access accounts are excluded from all policies and monitored.
questions.stem: Which THREE findings should you flag as gaps against Zero Trust? Select THREE.
options: The broad VIP group exclusion from MFA
Legacy authentication isn't blocked
Admin roles don't require phishing-resistant MFA
Emergency access accounts are excluded and monitored
Policies are named by persona
questions.explain: Broad exclusions, unblocked legacy auth (which can't do MFA) and weak MFA for admins all break 'verify explicitly'. Excluding monitored emergency access accounts is recommended to avoid lockout, and persona-based naming is Microsoft's recommended practice.

questions.stem: Before enforcing a new Conditional Access policy, you want to see which existing policies would apply to a specific user signing in to a specific app from a given location, without the user signing in. What should you use?
options: Report-only mode
The Conditional Access What If tool
Sign-in logs
Access reviews
questions.explain: The What If tool simulates a sign-in with chosen user, app and conditions and lists the policies that would apply. Report-only and sign-in logs require real sign-ins to occur, and access reviews attest to access rather than evaluating policy.

questions.stem: You are writing AD DS hardening requirements. Which THREE should you include? Select THREE.
options: Deploy Windows LAPS to give every workstation and server a unique, rotated local administrator password
Use group managed service accounts (gMSA) for services
Install Microsoft Defender for Identity sensors on domain controllers and AD CS servers
Add all service accounts to the Protected Users group
Enable SMBv1 for compatibility on domain controllers
questions.explain: LAPS stops lateral movement with shared local admin passwords, gMSAs give long automatically rotated service passwords, and Defender for Identity detects identity attacks on DCs and AD CS. Protected Users breaks service accounts (no delegation or NTLM), and SMBv1 should be disabled.

questions.stem: You need Domain Admin accounts to be unable to use NTLM, unconstrained delegation or RC4 Kerberos encryption, with minimal configuration effort. What should you do?
options: Configure a fine-grained password policy for the admins
Enable Windows LAPS for the admin accounts
Add the accounts to the Protected Users security group
Mark the accounts as gMSAs
questions.explain: Protected Users membership automatically blocks NTLM, delegation and weak Kerberos encryption types for its members and shortens TGT lifetime. Fine-grained password policies set password rules, LAPS manages local (not domain) admin passwords, and gMSA is for service accounts, not people.
